claim: Two-color fluorescence co-localization in 3D has the potential to achieve accurate measurements at the nanometer length scale.
source: Two-color fluorescence co-localization in 3D (three-dimension) has the potential to achieve accurate measurements at the nanometer length scale.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general capability of the method.

claim: The optimized 3D fluorescence co-localization method yields mean separation with ~10 nm accuracy between green and red fluorescently labeled protein epitopes within single human kinetochores.
source: Here, we optimized a 3D fluorescence co-localization method that uses mean values for chromatic aberration correction to yield the mean separation with ~10 nm accuracy between green and red fluorescently labeled protein epitopes within single human kinetochores.
evidence: The abstract states the method achieves ~10 nm accuracy, which is supported by experimental data and computer simulations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Accuracy depends critically on achieving small standard deviations in fluorescence centroid determination.
source: Accuracy depended critically on achieving small standard deviations in fluorescence centroid determination, chromatic aberration across the measurement field, and coverslip thickness.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by computer simulations showing how CDsd affects measurements.

claim: Accuracy depends critically on achieving small standard deviations in chromatic aberration across the measurement field.
source: Accuracy depended critically on achieving small standard deviations in fluorescence centroid determination, chromatic aberration across the measurement field, and coverslip thickness.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by computer simulations showing how CAsd affects measurements.

claim: Accuracy depends critically on achieving small standard deviations in coverslip thickness.
source: Accuracy depended critically on achieving small standard deviations in fluorescence centroid determination, chromatic aberration across the measurement field, and coverslip thickness.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing effects of different coverslip thicknesses.

claim: Large standard deviations in centroid determination, chromatic aberration, and coverslip thickness significantly increase 3D measurements from their true values.
source: Computer simulations showed that large standard deviations in these parameters significantly increase 3D measurements from their true values.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated through computer simulations in Figure 9.

claim: At metaphase, the protein linkage between CENP-A within the inner kinetochore and the microtubule-binding domain of the Ndc80 complex within the outer kinetochore is on average ~90 nm.
source: Our 3D results show that at metaphase, the protein linkage between CENP-A within the inner kinetochore and the microtubule-binding domain of the Ndc80 complex within the outer kinetochore is on average ~90 nm.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: The Ndc80 complex appears fully extended at metaphase.
source: The Ndc80 complex appears fully extended at metaphase and exhibits the same subunit structure in vivo as found in vitro by crystallography.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by measurements in Figure 4 showing the complex length matches in vitro measurements.

claim: The Ndc80 complex exhibits the same subunit structure in vivo as found in vitro by crystallography.
source: The Ndc80 complex appears fully extended at metaphase and exhibits the same subunit structure in vivo as found in vitro by crystallography.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by comparison of measurements in Figure 4 with published crystallography data.

claim: The maximum resolution of confocal light microscopy without image processing is ~200 nm in the x-y image plane.
source: Confocal light microscopy (LM) is widely used for understanding protein localization, architecture, and functions in cells, but the maximum resolution without any image processing is still only ~200 nm in the x-y image plane and ~400 nm along the z-axis.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the diffraction limit of light microscopy.

claim: The maximum resolution of confocal light microscopy without image processing is ~400 nm along the z-axis.
source: Confocal light microscopy (LM) is widely used for understanding protein localization, architecture, and functions in cells, but the maximum resolution without any image processing is still only ~200 nm in the x-y image plane and ~400 nm along the z-axis.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the diffraction limit of light microscopy.

claim: CENP-A within nucleosomes at centromeric chromatin marks the site of kinetochore assembly.
source: A modified histone H3, CENP-A, within nucleosomes at centromeric chromatin marks the site of kinetochore assembly.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about kinetochore biology.

claim: CENP-A recruits ~25 different kinds of core-structural proteins including CCAN proteins and KMN network proteins.
source: CENP-A recruits ~25 different kinds of core-structural proteins including Constitutive Centromere Associated Protein Network (CCAN) proteins and outer kinetochore proteins called the KMN network (Knl1, Mis12 complex, and Ndc80 complex) (Cheeseman et al., 2006; McKinley and Cheeseman, 2016; Musacchio and Desai, 2017; Pesenti et al., 2016; Takeuchi and Fukagawa, 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: CENP-C and CENP-T are important linkers in human kinetochores that connect between centromeric chromatin and the KMN network proteins.
source: Two important linkers in human kinetochores are CENP-C and CENP-T because they connect between centromeric chromatin and the KMN network proteins (Huis In 't Veld et al., 2016; Klare et al., 2015; Musacchio and Desai, 2017; Nishino et al., 2013; Nishino et al., 2012; Screpanti et al., 2011; Suzuki et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is one of the best structurally characterized kinetochore proteins.
source: The highly conserved Ndc80 complex (Hec1(Ndc80), Nuf2, Spc24, Spc25) is one of the best structurally characterized kinetochore proteins, and it has a major role in kinetochore microtubule (kMT) attachment (Ciferri et al., 2008; Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: The Ndc80 complex has a major role in kinetochore microtubule attachment.
source: The highly conserved Ndc80 complex (Hec1(Ndc80), Nuf2, Spc24, Spc25) is one of the best structurally characterized kinetochore proteins, and it has a major role in kinetochore microtubule (kMT) attachment (Ciferri et al., 2008; Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The Delta method provided local chromatic aberration correction in the x-y image plane by measurements along the K-K axis between pairs of sister kinetochores.
source: The Delta method provided local chromatic aberration (CA) correction in the x-y image plane by measurements along the K-K axis between pairs of sister kinetochores.
evidence: This describes the Delta method as reported in Wan et al., 2009.

claim: The CICADA method yielded an identical value to what was obtained by the Delta method.
source: More recently, Fuller and Straight (2012) developed a 3D method (termed CICADA [Co-localization and In-situ Correction of Aberration for Distance Analysis]) to measure the mean separation of red and green fluorescent centroids at individual kinetochores while locally correcting for CA in the x, y, and z directions using a third color (Fuller and Straight, 2012). Their method yielded an identical value to what was obtained by the Delta method (Fuller and Straight, 2012; Suzuki et al., 2014; Wan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations comparing the two methods.

claim: Smith et al., 2016 used a 3D measurement method to obtain mean separation values for protein domains within kinetochores that were significantly greater than Delta values and CICADA method values.
source: In contrast, a recent report by Smith et al., 2016 used a 3D measurement method to obtain mean separation values for protein domains within kinetochores that were significantly greater than our Delta values and the 3D value obtained by the CICADA method (Fuller and Straight, 2012; Smith et al., 2016; Suzuki et al., 2014; Wan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published values from Smith et al., 2016.

claim: Smith et al., 2016 questioned the accuracy and significance of the Delta values because they were '1D measurements and neglected z-axis information'.
source: This group questioned the accuracy and significance of the Delta values because they were '1D measurements and neglected z-axis information'.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the criticism from Smith et al., 2016.

claim: HeLa cells were grown on #1.5 coverslips to prevent Z-axis chromatic aberration.
source: HeLa cells were grown on #1.5 coverslips, the design value for the microscope objective, to prevent Z-axis CA (chromatic aberration) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as part of the sample preparation protocol.

claim: Cells were fixed with paraformaldehyde without pre-extraction or supplement of detergent in the PFA solution.
source: Cells were fixed with paraformaldehyde (PFA) without pre-extraction or supplement of detergent in the PFA solution, and stained with primary antibodies using a protocol from previous studies (Figure 1A) (Suzuki et al., 2015; Suzuki et al., 2014; Suzuki et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated as part of the fixation protocol.

claim: Integrated kinetochore fluorescence above background (>100,000 photon counts per kinetochore) was important to minimize the SD of centroid determination close to 5 nm.
source: Integrated kinetochore fluorescence above background (>100,000 photon counts per kinetochore) was important to minimize the SD of centroid determination (CDsd) close to 5 nm (Thompson et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated as a requirement for accurate measurements and supported by citation to Thompson et al., 2002.

claim: The mean values of CAx, CAy, and CAz were each very similar between different preparations.
source: Note the mean values for CAx, CAy, and CAz were each very similar between different preparations.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: PBS embedding has a refractive index near water, 1.33, and far from the refractive index of the coverslip (~1.52).
source: PBS has a refractive index near water, 1.33, and far from the refractive index of the coverslip (~1.52).
evidence: This is stated as a known property of PBS.

claim: PBS embedding produced a much larger SD for CAz compared to ProLong Gold (48 nm vs ~18 nm).
source: The major difference was a much larger SD for CAz compared to ProLong Gold (48 nm vs ~18 nm, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: The lower refractive index of PBS induces spherical aberration that increases with z-axis depth from the coverslip surface.
source: This occurs because the lower refractive index induces spherical aberration that increases with z-axis depth from the coverslip surface (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

source: Our mean separation ±SD between CENP-T (M) and Hec1-9G3 for Delta = 60 ± 7.5 nm, S(2D)=63 ± 11.2 nm, ML2D = 62 ± 11.3 nm, S(3D)=69 ± 12.3 nm, and ML3D = 66 ± 12.5 nm (Figure 3A–B), almost identical to the previous studies (Fuller and Straight, 2012; Suzuki et al., 2014; Wan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3.

source: Our mean separation ±SD between CENP-T (M) and Hec1-9G3 for Delta = 60 ± 7.5 nm, S(2D)=63 ± 11.2 nm, ML2D = 62 ± 11.3 nm, S(3D)=69 ± 12.3 nm, and ML3D = 66 ± 12.5 nm (Figure 3A–B), almost identical to the previous studies (Fuller and Straight, 2012; Suzuki et al., 2014; Wan et al., 2009).

evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3.

source: Our mean separation ±SD between CENP-T (M) and Hec1-9G3 for Delta = 60 ± 7.5 nm, S(2D)=63 ± 11.2 nm, ML2D = 62 ± 11.3 nm, S(3D)=69 ± 12.3 nm, and ML3D = 66 ± 12.5 nm (Figure 3A–B), almost identical to the previous studies (Fuller and Straight, 2012; Suzuki et al., 2014; Wan et al., 2009).

evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3.

source: For CENP-T(M) to Hec1-9G3, the mean vector angle to the K-K axis in the X-Y plane, angle α = −0.3 ± 20.1 degrees, while the mean vector angle relative to the Z-axis (angle β) was −1.8 ± 23.3 degrees (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The Ndc80 complex contour length is 55 ~ 60 nm, as measured in vitro by electron microscopy and crystallography.
source: Most of the length of the Ndc80 complex is alpha helical coiled-coil, and its contour length is 55 ~ 60 nm, as measured in vitro by electron microscopy and crystallography (Ciferri et al., 2008; Huis In 't Veld et al., 2016; Valverde et al., 2016; Wei et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: The mean separation measurements between Spc25-EGFP and Hec1-9G3 were Delta = 49 ± 5 nm, S(2D)=52 ± 10 nm, S(3D)=55 ± 10 nm, ML2D = 51 ± 10 nm, and ML3D = 53 ± 10 nm.
source: For example, the mean separation measurements between Spc25-EGFP and Hec1-9G3 were Delta = 49 ± 5 nm, S(2D)=52 ± 10 nm, S(3D)=55 ± 10 nm, ML2D = 51 ± 10 nm, and ML3D = 53 ± 10 nm.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: The Ndc80 complex is likely extended along kMTs since the Delta and ML3D values for the length of the Ndc80 complex are nearly identical.
source: The Ndc80 complex is likely extended along kMTs since the Delta and ML3D values for the length of the Ndc80 complex are nearly identical.
evidence: This is an inference based on the similarity of Delta and ML3D measurements.

claim: The C-terminus of Spc24 is located a few nm inside of the C-terminus of Spc25.
source: As expected, the C-terminus of Spc24 is located a few nm inside of the C-terminus of Spc25, and Spc24 is longer than Spc25 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) (Valverde et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and citation to Valverde et al., 2016.

claim: Spc24 is longer than Spc25.
source: As expected, the C-terminus of Spc24 is located a few nm inside of the C-terminus of Spc25, and Spc24 is longer than Spc25 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) (Valverde et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and citation to Valverde et al., 2016.

claim: The CH-domain of Nuf2 is located a few nm inside of the N-terminal CH domain of Ndc80.
source: The CH-domain of Nuf2 is located a few nm inside of the N-terminal CH domain of Ndc80, and Ndc80 is longer than Nuf2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) (Ciferri et al., 2008; Valverde et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and citations.

claim: Ndc80 is longer than Nuf2.
source: The CH-domain of Nuf2 is located a few nm inside of the N-terminal CH domain of Ndc80, and Ndc80 is longer than Nuf2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1) (Ciferri et al., 2008; Valverde et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1 and citations.

claim: In vivo, the C-terminus of Ndc80 locates much closer to the globular domains of Spc24/Spc25 than expected from in vitro structures.
source: Unexpectedly, in vivo, the C-terminus of Ndc80 locates much closer to the globular domains of Spc24/Spc25 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The difference in C-terminus Ndc80 position might be caused by structural restrictions on the position of the EGFP tag.
source: This difference might be caused by structural restrictions on the position of the EGFP tag, which was tethered to the protein end by a nine amino acid linker.
evidence: This is speculation about the cause of the observed difference.

claim: Selection of sister pairs did not influence measurements, as random kinetochore selection produced nearly identical mean separation values.
source: To test if selection of sister pairs influenced our measurements, we measured 120 kinetochores selected randomly in a single metaphase cell. This produced a mean separation value nearly identical to the mean value for single kinetochore measurements of sister pairs obtained from six metaphase cells (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: All 2D and Delta values are nearly identical (usually less than 3 nm difference).
source: All of our 2D and Delta values are nearly identical (usually less than 3 nm difference).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: 3D measurements were only ~5 nm larger than the Delta or 2D values.
source: In general, our 3D measurements were only ~5 nm larger than the Delta or 2D values (Figure 5 and the Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5 and Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: The 3D mean separation between CENP-A and Hec1-9G3 is ~90 nm.
source: For example, our 3D mean separation between CENP-A and Hec1-9G3 is ~90 nm, which is nearly identical to values obtained by Delta (~84 nm) and ML2D (~85 nm).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 5.

source: Coverslip thickness both greater and less than 0.17 mm produces z-axis chromatic aberration (Z-offset) independent of focal depth
evidence: This is stated as a section heading and supported by experimental data in Table 3.

claim: The mean Z-offset for CENP-T(M) to Hec1-9G3 showed ~±10 nm for #1.5 coverslips.
source: The mean Sz (Z-offset) for CENP-T(M) to Hec1-9G3 showed ~±10 nm for #1.5 coverslips, −29 to −19 nm for #1 coverslips, and 29 to 46 nm for # 2 (Table 3B).

claim: The mean Z-offset for CENP-T(M) to Hec1-9G3 showed −29 to −19 nm for #1 coverslips.
source: The mean Sz (Z-offset) for CENP-T(M) to Hec1-9G3 showed ~±10 nm for #1.5 coverslips, −29 to −19 nm for #1 coverslips, and 29 to 46 nm for # 2 (Table 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 3B.

claim: The mean Z-offset for CENP-T(M) to Hec1-9G3 showed 29 to 46 nm for #2 coverslips.
source: The mean Sz (Z-offset) for CENP-T(M) to Hec1-9G3 showed ~±10 nm for #1.5 coverslips, −29 to −19 nm for #1 coverslips, and 29 to 46 nm for # 2 (Table 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 3B.

claim: The mean thickness of #1.5 coverslips was 0.17 mm with a range of 0.16 to 0.19 mm.
source: We measured their thickness with a micrometer, and the mean value was 0.17 mm with a range of 0.16 to 0.19 (Figure 6, n > 100).

claim: For #1 coverslips, the mean thickness was 0.15 mm.

claim: For #2 coverslips, the mean thickness was 0.22 mm.
source: For #1 coverslips, the mean was 0.15 mm and for #2 coverslips it was 0.22 mm (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 6.

claim: Unusually large Z-offset values (>25 nm) were largely produced by coverslip thicknesses much thinner or thicker than 0.17 mm.
source: Based on these experimental results, we suspect that unusually large Z-offset values (>25 nm) measured in our experiments (Figure 5—source data 1) were largely produced by coverslip thicknesses much thinner or thicker than 0.17 mm.

claim: Both CENP-T(M) and Hec1-9G3 signal levels in GA fixation samples were significantly reduced by ~35% to 60% compared to PFA fixation.
source: Interestingly, both CENP-T(M) and Hec1-9G3 signal levels in GA fixation samples (Methods 4–7) were significantly reduced by ~35% to 60% compared to PFA fixation (Method 1), PFA with detergent fixation (by 20–30%), or MeOH fixation (~20%) (Figure 7B).

claim: GA fixation significantly reduced the signal to noise ratio compared to PFA or MeOH fixation.

evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: There were no significant differences in mean separation between PFA fixation and GA fixation.

evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 5.

claim: Significant shrinkage was observed when samples were fixed by Methods 3, 8, and 9.
source: However, we observed significant shrinkage when samples were fixed by Methods 3, 8, and 9 (Table 5).

evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 5.

claim: The standard PFA fixation method (Method 1) did not produce any shrinkage.

source: Smith et al., 2016 reported that the mean 3D separation between endogenous CENP-A and the C-terminus of Ndc80 was 81.7 ± 0.7 nm SEM (n = 3302, SD =±40 nm), about 42 nm larger than our measured value of 40 nm ± ~ 10 nm (SD) (Table 7).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Table 7.

claim: The CDsd from Smith et al., 2016 was estimated to be about five times larger than the current study's values (22 nm, 22 nm, and 44 nm compared to 4 nm, 4 nm and 8 nm in the x, y and z directions).
source: This analysis yielded values for CDsd about five times larger than ours (22 nm, 22 nm, and 44 nm compared to 4 nm, 4 nm and 8 nm in the x, y and z directions) (Figure 9—source data 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9—source data 1.

claim: The reported CAsd from Smith et al., 2016 was significantly larger than the current study's values (26 nm, 23 nm and 43 nm compared to 9 nm, 7.5 nm and 18 nm in the x, y and z directions).
source: Their reported CAsd was also significantly larger than ours (26 nm, 23 nm and 43 nm compared to 9 nm, 7.5 nm and 18 nm in the x, y and z directions) (Smith et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citation to Smith et al., 2016.

claim: Simulations using the estimated CDsd and reported CAsd from Smith et al., 2016 produce results nearly identical to their mean separation measurements.
source: Results of simulations in Figure 9D using the values we estimated for their CDsd and their reported CAsd produce results nearly identical to their mean separation measurements, and show how the differences in the SDs between their and our measurements could be responsible for their much larger values.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9D.

claim: The higher levels of CDsd and CAsd in Smith et al., 2016 are likely responsible for the very large SDs they measured for the angles α and β compared to the current study.
source: In addition, the higher levels for CDsd and CAsd are likely responsible for the very large SDs they measured for the angles α and β compared to ours (Figure 9E).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9E.

claim: Human kinetochores are built from multiple copies of core-kinetochore proteins.
source: Human kinetochores are built from multiple copies of core-kinetochore proteins (Suzuki et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Suzuki et al., 2015.

claim: The accuracy of separation measurements is sensitive to the spatial staggering of the labeled molecules along the kinetochore inner to outer axis only for stagger greater than 200 nm.
source: A previous study has shown that the accuracy of separation measurements is sensitive to the spatial staggering of the labeled molecules along the kinetochore inner to outer axis only for stagger greater than 200 nm, which has the possibility of producing two fluorescent peaks instead of a single peak if staggering is not random (Joglekar et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Joglekar et al., 2009.

claim: All kinetochores labeled by specific antibodies or EGFP exhibited a Gaussian distribution with a single peak.
source: All kinetochores labeled by specific antibodies or EGFP in our study exhibited a Gaussian distribution with a single peak.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the experimental data.

claim: Centroid measurements correspond to the mean position of the fluorescently labeled protein epitopes within human kinetochores.
source: This indicates that our centroid measurements correspond to the mean position of the fluorescently labeled protein epitopes within human kinetochores.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of single-peaked Gaussian distributions.

claim: Mean measurements of individual kinetochores within a single cell yielded the identical value at metaphase as the mean obtained from kinetochores within six different cells.
source: First, we found that mean measurements of individual kinetochores (not sister pairs) within a single cell yielded the identical value at metaphase as the mean obtained from kinetochores (sister pairs) within six different cells (Table 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 2.

claim: Only 10–15 kinetochores were needed to be averaged to achieve the mean and SD typical of >150 kinetochores.
source: Second, as expected for the Gaussian distribution measured for separation values (e.g. Figure 3B), we found that only 10–15 kinetochores were needed to be averaged to achieve the mean and SD typical of >150 kinetochores (Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: A significant part of the SD in 2D/3D measurements must be from the CDsd and CAsd and not from differences between kinetochores.
source: Third, the SD of our 2D/3D measurements are small, typically less than 12 nm, and a significant part of this SD must be from the CDsd and CAsd (Table 6A and see above discussion) and not from differences between kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by simulation results in Table 6A.

claim: Ksd of about ±5 nm or less plus measurement CDsd and CAsd yielded the experimental mean SD value of 12.5 nm.
source: Simulation results showed that Ksd of about ±5 nm or less plus measurement CDsd and CAsd yielded the experimental mean SD value of 12.5 nm (Figure 9—source data 2).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9—source data 2.

claim: The vast majority of kinetochores at metaphase have a similar protein architecture.
source: These results imply that the vast majority of kinetochores at metaphase have a similar protein architecture.
evidence: This is an inference based on the simulation results showing low kinetochore-to-kinetochore variability.

claim: PFA fixation does not shrink kinetochore structure and produces exactly the same Delta, 2D, and 3D mean separation values obtained by GA fixation.
source: We found that our PFA fixation does not shrink kinetochore structure and produces exactly the same Delta, 2D, and 3D mean separation values obtained by the GA fixation.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Table 5.

claim: A major problem with GA fixation is that it interferes with antibody labeling, preventing immunofluorescence with many antibodies, and reduced fluorescence for others.
source: A major problem with GA fixation is that it interferes with antibody labeling, preventing immunofluorescence with many antibodies, and reduced fluorescence for others like those used in Figure 7.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Primary GA fixation may not be suitable for analysis of molecular distribution by immuno-electron microscopy because of poor recognition by antibodies.
source: In addition, our data indicate that primary GA fixation may not be suitable for analysis of molecular distribution by immuno-electron microscopy because of poor recognition by antibodies.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed reduction in antibody binding with GA fixation.

claim: For immuno-electron microscopy, GA fixation should be used as the post-fixation solution, but only after the antibody reaction has been performed.
source: For immuno-electron microscopy, GA fixation should be used as the post-fixation solution, but only after the antibody reaction has been performed.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the findings about GA fixation effects on antibody binding.

claim: The optimized 3D fluorescence co-localization method can achieve ~10 nm accuracy for mean separations larger than 18 nm.
source: This study provides an optimized 3D fluorescence co-localization method with error analysis. It can achieve ~10 nm accuracy for mean separations larger than 18 nm.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by experimental data and simulations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Mean 3D fluorescence co-localization measurements for human kinetochore protein architecture are close to the mean values obtained using local correction of CA.
source: Our mean 3D fluorescence co-localization measurements for human kinetochore protein architecture are close to the mean values obtained using local correction of CA (Wan et al., 2009; Fuller and Straight, 2012) and successfully predict the known structural lengths of the Ndc80 complex components (Ciferri et al., 2008; Valverde et al., 2016; Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by comparison with published values.

claim: The measurements successfully predict the known structural lengths of the Ndc80 complex components.
source: Our mean 3D fluorescence co-localization measurements for human kinetochore protein architecture are close to the mean values obtained using local correction of CA (Wan et al., 2009; Fuller and Straight, 2012) and successfully predict the known structural lengths of the Ndc80 complex components (Ciferri et al., 2008; Valverde et al., 2016; Musacchio and Desai, 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by comparison with published structural data.

claim: The optimized 3D co-localization method is a useful tool for broad research fields that need to determine mean protein architecture with nm-accuracy.
source: This optimized 3D co-localization method is a useful tool for broad research fields that need to determine mean protein architecture with nm-accuracy.
evidence: This is a concluding statement about the utility of the method.

claim: There was a gradient for CAx in the x direction (~30 nm/ 280 pixels (19 µm)), but not in the y or z directions.
source: In the measurement region, there was a gradient for CAx in the x direction (~30 nm/ 280 pixels (19 µm)), but not in the y or z directions.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: There was a gradient for CAy in the y direction (~21 nm/180 pixels (11.5 µm)), but not in the x or z directions.
source: There was a gradient for CAy in the y direction (~21 nm/180 pixels (11.5 µm)), but not in the x or z directions.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: There was no noticeable gradient for CAz in either the x, y, or z directions compared to the SD.
source: There was no noticeable gradient for CAz in either the x, y, or z directions compared to the SD (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The gradients in CA had no more effect on measurement accuracy than randomly distributed CA values with the same mean and SD.
source: These gradients in CA had no more effect on measurement accuracy than randomly distributed CA values with the same mean and SD (see computer simulations below).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by computer simulations.

claim: Z-offset is a major source of error only if it is not produced by the specimen.
source: Z-offset is a major source of error only if it is not produced by the specimen.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle about Z-offset.

claim: It is not recommended to subtract Z-offset from Sz data since there could be a specimen contribution.
source: As a general rule, we do not recommend subtracting Z-offset from Sz data since there could be a specimen contribution.
evidence: This is stated as a recommendation based on the analysis of Z-offset.

claim: Only absolute values of Z-offset >30 nm make 3D mean separation measurements significantly larger.
source: Computer simulations of the measurement method showed that only absolute values of Z-offset >30 nm make 3D mean separation measurements significantly larger (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 9C.

claim: The method produces nearly identical results from multiple samples.
source: Also, our method produces nearly identical results from multiple samples.
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by data showing consistency across samples.

claim: Imaging was performed using a confocal light microscope with a high NA objective lens (100x/1.4 NA) and a camera with small pixel size (64 nm).
source: Imaging was performed using a confocal light microscope with a high NA objective lens (100x/1.4 NA) and a camera with small pixel size (64 nm, less than 1/3 resolution limit) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated as part of the imaging protocol.

claim: Images were recorded at 200 nm intervals along the z-axis.
source: Images were recorded at 200 nm intervals along the z-axis beginning just before the coverslip surface and extending to the top of the spindle to measure equal numbers of kinetochores below and above the middle of the spindle.
evidence: This is stated as part of the imaging protocol.

claim: The concentration of green and red secondary antibodies was adjusted to give nearly equal fluorescence intensity.
source: The concentration of green and red secondary antibodies was adjusted to give nearly equal fluorescence intensity (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated as part of the staining protocol.

claim: Labeled samples were typically mounted with ProLong Gold mounting media.
source: Labeled samples were typically mounted with ProLong Gold mounting media.
evidence: This is stated as part of the sample preparation protocol.

claim: A monoclonal antibody (9G3) was used to label Hec1 (hsNdc80) protein at a site just inside of its MT binding CH domain.
source: For the cellular CA correction standard, a monoclonal antibody (9G3) was used to label Hec1 (hsNdc80) protein at a site just inside of its MT binding CH domain, and this antibody was double labeled with green and red fluorescence by secondary antibodies (called Hec1-9G3-GR).
evidence: This is stated as part of the CA correction method.

claim: The 9G3 antibody was double labeled with green and red fluorescence by secondary antibodies (called Hec1-9G3-GR).
source: For the cellular CA correction standard, a monoclonal antibody (9G3) was used to label Hec1 (hsNdc80) protein at a site just inside of its MT binding CH domain, and this antibody was double labeled with green and red fluorescence by secondary antibodies (called Hec1-9G3-GR).
evidence: This is stated as part of the CA correction method.

claim: The x, y, z coordinates for the centroids of green and red were obtained using 3D Gaussian fitting methods.
source: For each kinetochore, we obtained the x, y, z coordinates for the centroids of green (Xg, Yg, Zg) and red (Xr, Yr, Zr) using 3D Gaussian fitting methods (Wan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as part of the image analysis method and supported by citation.

claim: The Sx, Sy, and Sz coordinates of the separation vector S were calculated from Sx = Xg-Xr-meanCAx (CAmx), Sy = Yg-Yr-meanCAy (CAmy), and Sz = Zg-Zr-meanCAz (CAmz).
source: The Sx, Sy, and Sz coordinates of the separation vector S between green and red foci were calculated from Sx = Xg-Xr-meanCAx (CAmx), Sy = Yg-Yr-meanCAy (CAmy), and Sz = Zg-Zr-meanCAz (CAmz) (Figure 1E), where the mean values of CAx, CAy, and CAz were obtained from kinetochores labeled with Hec1-9G3-GR within our measurement volume (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated as part of the image analysis method.

claim: 'Raw' values for the mean separation vector lengths in 2D and 3D were calculated as S(2D) = mean ((Sx2 + Sy2)0.5) and S(3D) = mean ((Sx2 + Sy2 + Sz2)0.5).
source: 'Raw' values for the mean separation vector lengths in 2D and 3D were calculated for each pair of green-red kinetochore labels as S(2D) = mean ((Sx2 + Sy2)0.5) and S(3D) = mean ((Sx2 + Sy2 + Sz2)0.5) from measurements of 200 to 400 kinetochores obtained from 5 to 20 different cells (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated as part of the image analysis method.

claim: The mean of 'raw' separation values (S(2D), and S(3D)) were over-estimates.
source: The mean of these 'raw' separation values (S(2D), and S(3D)) were over-estimates (Churchman et al., 2006; Churchman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations.

claim: A maximum likelihood method was applied to the raw separation data to obtain more accurate mean separation values (called ML2D and ML3D).
source: In order to obtain more accurate mean separation values, a maximum likelihood method was applied to the raw separation data (called ML2D and ML3D) (Churchman et al., 2006; Churchman et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by citations.
